purpose: same-pool, same-panel, same-scorer, same-budget comparison against three representative published-method styles; closes the external-baseline gap for the top-venue version
naming_rule: all baselines labeled '-style' with the sentence 'adapted to the same frozen model pool, task panel, scorer, and budget constraints'; no claim of faithful reproduction of the original published systems
budget_rule: same as frozen arms: per-task budget = max(200, 1.2 x static realized tokens); violations reported

RouteLLM_style_learned_query_router.training: 900-task finance profiling corpus (capability_profiling/): per-task propagated outcomes for medium/large recomputed with the frozen scorer from frozen RESPONSES (replay-level, zero calls); binary label = large-beats-medium on the task's propagated chain
RouteLLM_style_learned_query_router.features: 3584-d GTE-Qwen2-7B question embeddings (frozen encoder, CPU); train embeddings from PROFILE_EMB.npz aligned by question text
RouteLLM_style_learned_query_router.model: L2-regularized logistic regression (sklearn), 5-fold sanity on training corpus
RouteLLM_style_learned_query_router.inference: embed each panel query -> predict -> route to medium or large -> reuse the EXISTING mono cell of the chosen model (zero new model calls)
RouteLLM_style_learned_query_router.note: original RouteLLM routes strong/weak models by learned preference; here adapted to the frozen two-model pool and panels

FrugalGPT_style_cascade.policy: run the cheaper model (medium) first; escalate to large iff the deployable confidence check fails; stop after large
FrugalGPT_style_cascade.finance_check: answer extractable and finite (regex Answer: <number> / trailing number)
FrugalGPT_style_cascade.code_check: extracted unit tests pass in sandbox
FrugalGPT_style_cascade.cells: reuses existing medium and large mono cells for every panel task (zero new model calls)
FrugalGPT_style_cascade.cost_accounting: medium cost + large cost iff escalated

SelfRefine_style_iterative_refinement.finance: initial = existing large mono answer; feedback = self-critique prompt (same large model: state errors in the draft, give a corrected boxed answer); one critique+revise round; final scored by frozen scorer
SelfRefine_style_iterative_refinement.code: initial = existing large mono code; feedback = sandbox test failure report (deployable, deterministic); revise with the same model; at most 2 revisions; final scored by unit tests

reference_arms.Always_Large: existing frozen mono-large arm on each panel
reference_arms.Dynamic_DAG: existing frozen dynamic_real arm (decomposition_benchmark DAG-L/M for finance? NO - finance dynamic reference = multidag panels are a different panel; on the TAT-QA 200 panel the DAG reference = DAG-L/M; code reference = mbpp dynamic_real 80.0%

metrics: paired dQ vs Always-Large and vs the frozen DAG/Dynamic arm
constraints: no modification of any existing frozen result, protocol, scorer, or panel
no gold at runtime; all feedback deployable
one-shot; no post-hoc tuning of router/cascade/refine after results
